name: Friends of Figma, Lagos
reason_for_fit: Lagos chapter of Figma's official community programme, roughly 2,000 members, all of whom work in Figma and design for a Nigerian audience — the exact overlap of the Community file and the plugin.
suggested_angle: Offer a short walkthrough at a chapter event: the 24px grid, the 16px proof strip, and why three weights are struck through in the plugin picker.
notes: High confidence. Contact via the chapter page's organiser links; do not DM individual organisers cold.

name: Friends of Figma, Ibadan
reason_for_fit: Second Nigerian Figma chapter outside Lagos; a set drawn for Nigerian products is directly usable by its members and the chapter is small enough that a specific offer gets read.
suggested_angle: Same as Lagos but framed for a smaller room: bring the proof strip and ask what is missing from the backlog.
notes: High confidence — chapter page confirmed live.

name: Friends of Figma, Uyo
reason_for_fit: Third confirmed Nigerian chapter. Regional chapters surface concepts a Lagos-centric backlog will miss, which is exactly the input the project needs.
suggested_angle: Ask directly: what object do you keep redrawing that is not in the set?
notes: High confidence. Lower priority only because of size, not fit.

name: Friends of Figma, Nairobi
reason_for_fit: Roughly 900 members in Kenya. Relevant precisely because the library is Nigeria-first — the honest pitch is region as a first-class axis, not a claim to cover Kenya.
suggested_angle: Lead with the region-tagging question: how should a first Kenyan pass be scoped, and who would define it?
notes: High confidence. Do not imply the set covers East Africa; it does not.

name: Friends of Figma, Accra
reason_for_fit: Ghanaian chapter, and the library has a concrete open question that belongs to Ghana: kente-cloth sits in the backlog and 'ayo vs oware' is an unresolved rename from the audit.
suggested_angle: Ask them to settle ayo/oware and how kente-cloth should be region-tagged. A real question, not an announcement.
notes: Facebook page confirmed; check whether the chapter has moved to friends.figma.com before sending.

name: Friends of Figma Africa
reason_for_fit: Umbrella account for the African Figma chapters — one contact that reaches several chapters at once, and its stated purpose is making design resources accessible across Africa.
suggested_angle: Offer the Community file as a resource for chapters to use in workshops, with the grid page as teaching material.
notes: High confidence. Best contacted after individual chapters, so it is not the first they hear of it.

name: Figma Africa
reason_for_fit: Publication run by the Figma Africa community; it publishes practitioner write-ups rather than news, which fits a piece about the audit and the validator far better than a launch note.
suggested_angle: Offer a written piece: 'What auditing 86 African icons taught us about icon systems'. No product pitch in the body.
notes: Confirmed publication. Check last publish date — cadence has been irregular.

name: IxDF Lagos
reason_for_fit: Lagos UX/product-design local group with a mix of professionals and students; the students are the audience most likely to adopt an MIT icon set with no procurement conversation.
suggested_angle: Offer a session on icon-system fundamentals using the library as the worked example — grid, live area, counters at 16px.
notes: Confirmed group page. Events are organiser-led; propose a topic rather than a product demo.

name: GDG Lagos
reason_for_fit: Developer and designer community in Lagos running DevFest Lagos in November 2026. The React package and the generated-component pipeline are a developer story, distinct from the design one.
suggested_angle: Developer-framed: generated components, drift-checked in CI, tree-shakable imports, MIT. Time it to DevFest week.
notes: Confirmed. DevFest Lagos dates published for 13-14 November 2026 — verify before scheduling.

name: GDG Cloud Lagos
reason_for_fit: Second active Lagos GDG chapter with a separate audience from GDG Lagos; useful for a repeat without repeating yourself to the same room.
suggested_angle: The offline-by-build angle: a plugin whose privacy claim is a failing build rather than a policy document.
notes: Confirmed chapter page. Lower priority — cloud-focused audience, weaker fit.

name: Design Week Lagos
reason_for_fit: Nigeria's largest design festival, running 18-25 October 2026, and the week when the Nigerian design conversation is loudest. The library's phase 4 campaign is deliberately scheduled around it.
suggested_angle: Not a sponsorship approach. Offer the audit story as a talk or a written contribution to their programme coverage.
notes: Confirmed, dates published. Approach through the general contact form; we are not an exhibitor and should not imply otherwise.

name: Nairobi Design Week
reason_for_fit: Long-running East African design festival, 11th edition in March 2026, with a stated 2026 theme about honesty and imperfection in design — an unusually good match for a library that publishes its own backlog.
suggested_angle: Reference their theme directly and honestly: a set that ships less than it has drawn, and says why.
notes: Confirmed. March 2026 edition has passed; this is an approach for the next cycle, not this launch.

name: Design Week Africa
reason_for_fit: Pan-African design programme; the correct place to test whether the Nigeria-first framing reads as honest or as a shortfall before the library expands regionally.
suggested_angle: Ask rather than pitch: how should a Nigeria-first set describe itself without over-claiming the continent?
notes: Medium confidence on current activity — confirm the site is maintained before sending.

name: Design Indaba
reason_for_fit: The largest design-driven digital publication on the continent, running since 1995, with an editorial history of covering African design practice rather than African design products.
suggested_angle: The audit as a design-practice story: what an icon library is, and why this one ships less than it drew.
notes: Confirmed and long-established. Pitch the practice angle; a product announcement will not land there.

name: CcHUB Design Lab
reason_for_fit: CcHUB's design arm works on Nigerian public-interest products, which is precisely the context where a generic bowl standing in for jollof rice is a real usability problem rather than an aesthetic one.
suggested_angle: Framed around their own work: which objects have their teams had to redraw, and would those belong in the backlog?
notes: Confirmed. Approach through the general CcHUB contact route; do not cold-email named staff.

name: Design Hub Kampala
reason_for_fit: East African design co-working hub with a working designer membership; a good test of whether the region-as-first-class-axis architecture reads as credible outside Nigeria.
suggested_angle: Region tagging: what a Ugandan first pass would need, and who would confirm the names.
notes: AfriLabs profile confirmed; locate the hub's own current site before sending. Medium confidence.

name: Africa Design School
reason_for_fit: The first design school in West Africa, with Bachelor programmes in digital and graphic design — students who need a free, well-documented icon system and a worked example of a drawing spec.
suggested_angle: Offer the spec and the validator as teaching material. The library is a small enough system for a student to read end to end.
notes: URL is a World Design Organization reference page, not the school's own site — find and verify the official domain before sending. Medium confidence.

name: African Digital Art
reason_for_fit: A 17-year archive of African digital creative work that has published specifically on African typography and culture-driven type design, including Adinkra-derived typefaces — an editorial line that already covers this exact problem.
suggested_angle: The reference-set argument: every icon set encodes the vocabulary of whoever drew it, and this one names its own.
notes: Confirmed active with recent typography coverage. Strong fit.

name: Nataal
reason_for_fit: Global media brand covering contemporary African arts, design and culture, with a track record of profiling African design practice for an international readership.
suggested_angle: The cultural-naming process, not the icons: a library that refuses to name a cap it cannot identify.
notes: Confirmed. Fashion and art weighted — icons may be outside their remit. Low expectation, high value if it lands.

name: Open Source Community Africa
reason_for_fit: Over 5,000 African open-source contributors, explicitly including designers, and an organisation whose stated aim is raising credible African contributions to open source. The project's ask is a contribution ask.
suggested_angle: Lead with the contribution list: the cap that will not ship, the five unresolved renames, the 32-row name review.
notes: Confirmed. Also active at github.com/oscafrica and blog.oscafrica.org. Strongest single fit in the list.

name: She Code Africa
reason_for_fit: Non-profit with a large African women-in-tech membership and a documented open-source mentorship track run with OSCA — a route to first-time contributors for whom a small, well-documented repository is an ideal starting point.
suggested_angle: Frame the good-first-issue set honestly: the validator explains exactly which rule you broke, which makes a first PR tractable.
notes: Confirmed active site with chapters and events pages.

name: Open Source Design
reason_for_fit: A community specifically for designers working in open source, with a jobs board and a forum built around design contributions to OSS projects — the narrow intersection this project sits in.
suggested_angle: Post the design-contribution asks, not a release note. The forum audience responds to concrete tasks.
notes: Confirmed, with an active Discourse at discourse.opensourcedesign.net.

name: Design Systems Slack
reason_for_fit: The long-running open Slack for design-systems practitioners; the validator-and-provenance model is directly reusable by people there, independent of whether they need African icons.
suggested_angle: Share the approach, not the icons: executable promises, drift gates, and a weight rule that fails the build.
notes: Confirmed. Read the channel rules first — self-promotion norms vary by channel.

name: zheroes
reason_for_fit: Design-systems Slack community run by zeroheight and open to non-customers; heavy on token, component and governance discussion, where 'how do you stop a spec drifting' is a live question.
suggested_angle: The generated-output drift gate: committed generated code plus a CI check that fails if it diverges from its inputs.
notes: Confirmed invite page. Vendor-run community — keep the post tool-agnostic.

name: YorubaNames
reason_for_fit: A documentation project for Yorùbá names run by linguists and volunteer developers, founded by Kọ́lá Túbọ̀sún, with an open API and a submissions process. The library has two pending Yorùbá names and zero confirmed ones.
suggested_angle: The narrow question first: gangan or dùndún for the drum we drew. Then the 32-row list.
notes: Confirmed, with a public contact page. Highest-value contact in the entire list. Offer payment.

name: Igbo API / Nkọwa okwu
reason_for_fit: An open-source Igbo-English dictionary and API with thousands of entries and dialect variations — an organisation already solving the exact problem of recording a name with its variation rather than flattening it.
suggested_angle: Ask how they model dialect variation, then ask whether anyone would review the Igbo rows.
notes: Project confirmed via independent coverage; the exact domain was not verified in research — check before sending. Offer payment.

name: Masakhane
reason_for_fit: Grassroots African NLP collective with over 2,000 members and published datasets across Nigerian languages; a community where 'we have zero confirmed local names and will not guess' is an argument that needs no explanation.
suggested_angle: Frame the metadata review-state field as a data-quality decision, and ask for reviewers for Hausa and Igbo rows.
notes: Confirmed GitHub org and community docs. Contact via the community repository, not individual researchers.

name: Lanfrica
reason_for_fit: A catalogue of African language resources; a confirmed local-name set with review states attached would be a listable resource, and their audience is the reviewer pool the project needs.
suggested_angle: Offer the local-names dataset as a resource once names are confirmed — not before.
notes: Confirmed. Approach only after at least one language is confirmed; there is nothing to list today.

name: Wikimedia community, Nigeria
reason_for_fit: Nigerian Wikimedia volunteers work daily on Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo content and on sourcing claims rather than asserting them — the same discipline the library applies to icon names.
suggested_angle: The naming rule, told as a sourcing problem: an unverified referent is an unsourced claim.
notes: Exact user-group page not verified in research — search Meta for the current Nigerian user group before sending. Low confidence on URL, high confidence the group exists.

name: Iconify
reason_for_fit: Iconify aggregates 200+ open-source icon sets and has a documented submission process requiring an open licence and an automatable source — both of which this repository already satisfies.
suggested_angle: No pitch needed. Follow the documented submission requirements: public repo, MIT, automated updates.
notes: Confirmed submission documentation. Requires npm or a public git source, so this depends on phase 1 completing.

name: Iconduck
reason_for_fit: A search index of hundreds of open-source icon and illustration sets; inclusion puts the set in front of people searching for a specific object rather than for a library.
suggested_angle: Submit through their listed process. Emphasise the single licence across every asset.
notes: Ownership appears to have changed — the domain now surfaces under a commercial icon brand. Verify the submission route still exists before spending time on it.

name: SVG Repo
reason_for_fit: A large SVG search index used as a first stop by designers hunting a specific glyph; a searcher looking for 'danfo' will not find one anywhere else.
suggested_angle: Submit the set with the category structure intact so the Nigerian concepts are findable by name.
notes: Confirmed active. Check licence-display requirements before submitting.

name: Icônes
reason_for_fit: A fast icon browser built on Iconify's collections and widely used by front-end developers; inclusion here follows automatically from Iconify acceptance rather than needing a separate pitch.
suggested_angle: No separate outreach. Verify the set appears once Iconify accepts it.
notes: Confirmed. Downstream of the Iconify submission — track, do not pitch.

name: Iconbuddy
reason_for_fit: An open-source icon search engine indexing 300,000+ icons across sets; another surface where a specific-object search is the discovery path.
suggested_angle: Standard directory submission. No narrative required.
notes: Confirmed active. Likely downstream of Iconify; check before duplicating effort.

name: free-icon-resources
reason_for_fit: A curated GitHub list of 150+ free icon resources organised by type, including open-source sets and regional collections; a pull request is a legitimate, low-noise way in.
suggested_angle: Open a PR adding the set with an accurate one-line description. Do not overstate the count.
notes: Confirmed repository. Check the list's contribution rules; some curated lists reject self-submissions.

name: Prototypr
reason_for_fit: A design publication with a tools directory that already lists open-source icon resources, and an editorial history of publishing process pieces by the people who made the thing.
suggested_angle: Offer the process piece: from an 86-drawing audit to a validator that fails the build.
notes: Confirmed toolbox listings. Verify current editorial cadence before pitching.

name: Sidebar
reason_for_fit: Five hand-picked design links every weekday since 2012, with an open submission route; a single Sidebar placement reaches more working designers than most design publications.
suggested_angle: Submit the status page or the spec, not the home page. The unusual artefact is the one that gets picked.
notes: Confirmed, though the newsletter has taken breaks — verify it is publishing in the week you submit.

name: UX Collective
reason_for_fit: One of the largest design publications on the web with a weekly curated newsletter that regularly features design-systems and accessibility long-form writing.
suggested_angle: Submit the founder essay, not the launch. Their newsletter favours argument over product.
notes: Confirmed active. Both a publication and a newsletter — read submission guidelines for each.

name: TOOOLS.design
reason_for_fit: A curated directory and newsletter of design resources whose whole editorial purpose is surfacing free, well-made tools and asset libraries — the most direct match for an MIT icon set.
suggested_angle: Straight resource submission. Lead with MIT, one grid, one weight, and say the count plainly.
notes: Confirmed and actively publishing in 2026.

name: Figmalion
reason_for_fit: A weekly newsletter dedicated entirely to Figma, covering plugin launches and community files specifically — the single best-targeted newsletter for phase 2 and phase 3.
suggested_angle: Submit the plugin, and lead with the offline-by-build claim. That is the part that is unusual for a Figma plugin.
notes: Confirmed, weekly, with a public archive. Time the submission to plugin approval, not submission.

name: Product Disrupt
reason_for_fit: A long-running curated design newsletter with a published issue archive, favouring resources and process writing over news.
suggested_angle: The audit findings as a short read, with the library as the outcome rather than the subject.
notes: Confirmed with numbered issue archive.

name: Design Systems News
reason_for_fit: A design-systems newsletter still publishing in 2026; its readers are the people who care that a weight ships for the whole set or fails the build.
suggested_angle: The weight-completeness rule and the generated-output drift gate. Two paragraphs, no product framing.
notes: Confirmed active as of mid-2026.

name: Design Systems News (Onori)
reason_for_fit: A separate weekly design-systems editorial by PJ Onori with a strong bias toward opinionated writing about system design rather than tool announcements.
suggested_angle: Lead with the anti-claim: why we refuse to synthesise weights from stroke-width.
notes: Distinct from news.design.systems — confirm which is which before writing, they are easy to confuse.

name: Smashing Magazine
reason_for_fit: Publishes long, technical front-end and design-systems articles and has a standing interest in SVG practice; the analytic-bounds and currentColor material is genuinely publishable there on its own merits.
suggested_angle: Pitch an article on validating SVG icon sets in CI — bounds with curve extrema, allow-lists, drift gates. The library is the example.
notes: Confirmed. Follow their published author guidelines; this is an article pitch, not a press release.

name: It's Nice That
reason_for_fit: Runs a recurring 'The View From Lagos' strand covering Nigerian graphic design and type; a publication that has already decided this subject matters to its readers.
suggested_angle: The reference-set argument, told through Lagos: who decides what the default visual vocabulary contains.
notes: Confirmed with recent Lagos type-design coverage. Strong fit for the culture angle.

name: Creative Boom
reason_for_fit: A widely read creative-industry publication that regularly covers free and open resources for designers.
suggested_angle: Resource-led: MIT, no attribution, and a list of what has not been drawn.
notes: Confirmed. UK-weighted readership; treat as a secondary target.

name: AIGA Eye on Design
reason_for_fit: Editorial focus on design practice, labour and representation rather than product launches; the question of whose vocabulary an icon set encodes is squarely their subject.
suggested_angle: Who draws the default: a piece about the reference set inside every icon library.
notes: Confirm current publishing cadence before pitching — output has varied in recent years. Medium confidence.

name: Dezeen
reason_for_fit: Maintains an events guide that already lists Design Week Lagos and Nairobi Design Week, so African design programming is within their editorial scope.
suggested_angle: Only worth pitching alongside Design Week Lagos week. A standalone icon-library pitch will not land.
notes: Confirmed. Architecture and product weighted — low probability, listed for completeness.

name: Frontend Focus
reason_for_fit: A weekly HTML, CSS and browser-technology newsletter with a large front-end readership and an open link-submission route; SVG tooling is regular subject matter.
suggested_angle: Submit the spec or the validator write-up, not the icon browser. The technical artefact is what fits.
notes: Confirmed, weekly, curated by Chris Brandrick. Submissions via the site.

name: JavaScript Weekly
reason_for_fit: Same publisher as Frontend Focus with a much larger list; relevant because of the generated React package rather than the drawings.
suggested_angle: One line about hook-free generated components that work in Server Components, plus MIT.
notes: Confirmed publisher page. Weaker fit than Frontend Focus — submit to one, not both, in the same week.

name: Bytes
reason_for_fit: A large twice-weekly JavaScript newsletter with a conversational tone that suits an honest, self-deprecating framing of a small library.
suggested_angle: Lead with the number being small and the reason. That framing suits their voice better than a feature list.
notes: Confirmed active with a large subscriber base. Low probability of inclusion; cheap to try.

name: TLDR Design
reason_for_fit: A daily design digest aimed at a technical readership, which is the audience most likely to appreciate a CI-enforced spec.
suggested_angle: One-line submission: an icon library whose spec is a command, not a document.
notes: Verify the design edition is still running and find the current submission route. Medium confidence.

name: TechCabal
reason_for_fit: A pan-African technology publication that covers African product and design work, not only funding rounds; a Nigerian open-source release with a documented process is within its beat.
suggested_angle: The audit and the decision to ship less. Avoid framing it as a startup launch — it is not a company story.
notes: Confirmed and long-established. Pitch a named reporter who has covered design or open source, not the general desk.

name: Techpoint Africa
reason_for_fit: Nigeria's highest-traffic tech publication as of the 2026 rankings, with a public contact route and a readership of Nigerian product and engineering people — the direct users of this library.
suggested_angle: Nigerian product teams have been redrawing a danfo for years. Here is one, MIT, with the backlog published.
notes: Confirmed with a published contact page. Highest-reach African tech target in the list.

name: Condia
reason_for_fit: Formerly Benjamindada.com, with a stated focus on product reviews and analysis rather than announcements — a publication that will actually open the repository.
suggested_angle: Offer a hands-on review: install it, try to break the offline claim, tell readers what it cannot do.
notes: Confirmed rebrand from Benjamindada. Use the current name and domain; the old one still circulates.

name: Technext
reason_for_fit: Nigerian technology publication covering the local product ecosystem; a fourth outlet in the same market, useful for coverage breadth rather than depth.
suggested_angle: Same as Techpoint, shortened. Send after the first two have run or declined.
notes: Domain not directly verified in research — confirm before sending. Medium confidence.

name: Disrupt Africa
reason_for_fit: Pan-African startup and technology news with a long publishing history; broader African reach than the Nigeria-focused outlets.
suggested_angle: Frame the pan-African roadmap honestly: Nigeria first, region as a first-class field, kente-cloth still in the backlog.
notes: Confirm the exact domain — the publication has been referenced under more than one spelling. Medium confidence.

name: Built In Africa
reason_for_fit: Publishes profiles of African builders and their projects, including software engineers working on African language technology — the same territory as the library's naming problem.
suggested_angle: Profile angle: the decision to hold a valid drawing rather than name a cap nobody could identify.
notes: Confirmed via published articles on African language projects.

name: Rest of World
reason_for_fit: Reports on technology outside the Western default, and has a standing interest in how global software fails local contexts — which is exactly what a dollar sign in front of a naira figure is.
suggested_angle: The default-vocabulary story: what happens when the interface primitives were drawn somewhere else.
notes: Confirmed. Long lead times and a high bar; pitch the idea, not the product.

name: Zikoko
reason_for_fit: Nigeria's most widely shared youth-culture publication, with an audience that will recognise a danfo, a suya skewer and a ludo board instantly and has strong opinions about how they are drawn.
suggested_angle: Not a tech pitch. Offer the icons as a cultural artefact and invite readers to say which drawings are wrong.
notes: Confirmed. Tone matters enormously here — a corporate press release will be ignored or mocked.

name: Culture Custodian
reason_for_fit: A Nigerian youth-culture publication and digital archive founded in 2014, covering the objects and references this library draws.
suggested_angle: The archive framing: what it means to draw everyday Nigerian objects into a permanent, MIT-licensed set.
notes: Confirmed publication; verify current domain spelling before sending. Medium-high confidence.

name: The Republic
reason_for_fit: Long-form analysis of African politics, business and culture; the only outlet on this list likely to publish 2,000 words on who controls a default visual vocabulary.
suggested_angle: An essay commission, not coverage: representation as an infrastructure question rather than an aesthetic one.
notes: Confirm the exact domain before sending. Medium confidence. Long lead times.

name: The NATIVE
reason_for_fit: Nigerian youth-culture magazine with a strong design and visual-arts strand and an audience that overlaps heavily with young Nigerian designers.
suggested_angle: Visual-led: the drawings themselves, at size, with the objects named.
notes: Confirm the exact domain before sending. Medium confidence.

name: Show HN
reason_for_fit: A technical audience that responds well to a small, verifiable project with a documented constraint, and reliably interrogates claims like 'the build fails if fetch reaches the bundle'.
suggested_angle: Title it plainly: 'Show HN: Open-source icons for African life, validated in CI'. Be present in the thread all day.
notes: One shot only. Post after the website is live, never before. Expect scrutiny of the count — answer it honestly.

name: Product Hunt
reason_for_fit: A launch surface with a design-tools audience; the Figma plugin is the launchable artefact rather than the repository.
suggested_angle: Launch the plugin, not the library, and put the undrawn weights in the description rather than the comments.
notes: One shot only. Weak fit for open-source libraries with no commercial hook; low expectation.

name: Designer News
reason_for_fit: A designer-run link community where free, open resources are a recurring category.
suggested_angle: Straight link post with an honest one-line description including the count.
notes: Confirm activity levels before spending time — the community is quieter than it was.

name: DEV Community
reason_for_fit: A developer publishing platform with an active African developer readership and a norm of publishing build write-ups rather than announcements.
suggested_angle: Publish the technical write-up: analytic curve bounds, the element allow-list, and the drift gate.
notes: Confirmed and active. Cross-post the article rather than linking out.

name: r/web_design
reason_for_fit: A large web-design subreddit where free resource posts perform well when the poster is the maker and says so.
suggested_angle: Post as the maker, disclose it, lead with the limits. Read the subreddit's self-promotion rules first.
notes: Self-promotion rules are strictly enforced. If in doubt, do not post — a removal costs more than the post was worth.
